rendering.persona_description: Chidi is a 68-year-old retired civil engineer who spent thirty-five years inspecting bridges and municipal infrastructure before retiring four years ago. He and his wife Dolores have been married for forty-one years and live in the same split-level house they bought in 1987. He still consults part-time on a couple of small projects, plays cards with two old coworkers every other Thursday, and takes pride in being the guy who double-checks everyone else's math.
rendering.clinical_context: Chidi has no mental-health presentation. Every so often he has a passing thought about whether he truly loves Dolores, or whether their marriage was the right choice, the kind of ordinary unwanted thought most people have from time to time. These thoughts come and go on their own without lasting distress and without him doing anything to neutralize them; he shrugs them off and gets on with his day. He has never sought or needed any kind of evaluation or treatment related to this, since it isn't something he considers a problem.
rendering.behavioral_description: Chidi talks in a flat, matter-of-fact way, like he's presenting evidence rather than feelings, and he'll lay out the 'facts' of a situation as if building a case. He pushes back hard on anything that sounds like a directive, often restating advice back sarcastically before rejecting it, and he insists he can think through his own life without anyone telling him how to feel about his marriage. Once in a while a passing thought about his marriage crosses his mind, but he doesn't dwell on it, and he gets irritated when he feels managed or handled.

traits.living_situation: lives with his wife in a house they have owned since 1987
